News

New book · October 2026

Report · 9 October 2026

A full house in Bassano

Launch night · Libreria Palazzo Roberti, 9 October 2026

Libreria Palazzo Roberti filled up on Friday evening with friends, admirers, musicians and artists for the launch of Una vita dal vivo (Interno4 Edizioni), the book in which Carlo Casale looks back on fifty years of music, concerts and encounters in Italian rock. It was the second meeting of the Alta Fedeltà club, created by Francesco Nicolli and organised with Pick Up Records.

The conversation between Casale and journalist Filippo Bordignon was the heart of the evening. Bordignon opened by reading a passage from the book about its author. In his words, the best way to describe Carlo is this:

“Carlo Casale, a thinking mind with the courage to formulate original thoughts, has shown over his fifty years of artistic life how you can make rock while coming, geographically, from that Veneto (…) A man who has understood the necessary complexities of progress, and who has expanded his mind toward the infinite distances of music (…) the dissonant forms of punk and post-punk; who has understood the value of the constant beat, giving new flavours to club electronics.”

Then Casale spoke and the room listened. The talk moved between anecdotes, tour stories and memories from backstage. He went back to 1977, to the Outkids, to 1980 and the day he founded Frigidaire Tango with Stefano Dal Col. He told it plainly, and the audience followed, attentive and complicit, with laughter and applause.

Among those present were Stefano Dal Col, founder of Frigidaire Tango, and the band’s historic rhythm section, Maurizio Battistella (JM Le Baptiste) on drums and Diego Negrello on bass, along with other important musicians and artists from the scene.

When the talk ended, Casale signed copies of the book and records. Several collectors brought original Frigidaire Tango LPs for him to sign. One guest even brought an original ticket from the band’s first concert. Casale was visibly moved.

The night went on at Pick Up Records, where guests raised a glass, listened to Modern Vintage Wave and caught up with friends.

New book

Una vita dal vivo

by Carlo Casale · Charlie Out Cazale

Fifty years of music seen by a fan, musician, promoter and club manager. Carlo tells stories from Frigidaire Tango and The Vindicators, from backstage, and from Italian rock after 1977. The book has hundreds of original photos of his meetings with artists, from the Rolling Stones to the Chemical Brothers.

It comes with a CD of My Heart Brut, the last unreleased album by Charlie Out Cazale.

Since 1977

From the Outkids to Modern Vintage Wave

In July 1977 Carlo Casale came back from London and started a punk band, the Outkids, with guitarist Stefano Dal Col. The band became Trash, and once Marco Breda arrived on keyboards they became Frigidaire Tango. The name mixes the cult comics magazine Frigidaire with a word Casale added on impulse.

They sang in English under stage names (Charlie Out, Steve Hill, Mark Brenda, J.M. Le Baptiste). They mixed prog, krautrock and glam with punk energy and a cold synth edge. Their 1981 debut The Cock came out when they were all under 20. In 2010 the French magazine Tsugi named it one of the 100 essential lesser-known rock LPs.

A day in the studio cost 500,000 lire, a month's wages.

They toured Italy with The Sound. RAI 1 filmed them for the 1984 documentary L'ultimo concerto, and they played the Barcelona festival alongside Litfiba, Diaframma and CCCP. Then, after about thirty concerts, they played their last show on Treviso's city walls in July 1986.

Twenty years later the Freezer Box brought back the old material, and the trio started playing again. L'illusione del volo (2009), produced by Giorgio Canali, was their first album in Italian. A 20-artist tribute followed in 2013, and Modern Vintage Wave in 2026.

Timeline

1977 to today

  1. Jul 1977

    Carlo Casale and Stefano Dal Col form the punk band Outkids, after Casale comes back from a trip to London.

  2. 1979–80

    Renamed Trash, with Maurizio Battistella (drums) and Diego Negrello (bass). The 1980 demo tape for The Cock is recorded.

  3. 1980–81

    Marco Breda joins on keyboards and the band becomes Frigidaire Tango.

  4. 1981

    Debut LP The Cock (Young Records, YN/B 6006). Some sources date it 1982.

  5. 1983

    Franco Turesso joins as second keyboardist. Self-produced mini-LP Russian Dolls ("Recall", "Vanity Fair") with promo videos made by local TV. Italian tour with The Sound. RAI radio and TV slots on Orecchiocchio and Diskogenia.

  6. 1983–84

    Tracks on the Rockgarage Vol. 2 and Vol. 4 compilations. "Vanity Fair" appears on Rockerilla's Body Section.

  7. 1984

    RAI 1 documentary L'ultimo concerto, directed by Piergiorgio Gay.

  8. 1985

    Play the Biennale / Tendencias festival in Barcelona alongside Diaframma, Litfiba, CCCP and Avion Travel.

  9. 1986

    "The Romantic Lifeguard" on the Amnesty International P.E.A.C.E. compilation. Final concert on Treviso's city walls, July 1986.

  10. 1988–91

    Members run The Vindicators, a 1950s–60s rock'n'roll and R&B project.

  11. 2006–07

    The Freezer Box (Alma Records): 3 discs and a 50-page booklet, including the unreleased LP Music for Us and Live in Barcelona '85.

  12. 2008

    Reunion recordings with producer Giorgio Canali. Back on stage with Ran at La Gabbia, San Giorgio in Bosco (12 Jan).

  13. 2009

    L'illusione del volo (La Tempesta Dischi), their first album in Italian. About 15 live dates followed in 2010.

  14. Sep 2010

    French magazine Tsugi names The Cock one of the "100 essential lesser-known rock LPs".

  15. 2013

    Tribute album on Go Down Records. Synthetic Shadows reissues the 1980 demo tape on vinyl. Tribute concert at Maximum Festival, Zero Branco (TV).

  16. Jan 2026

    Single "Fears". "Non sei raggiungibile" follows in March.

  17. Apr–May 2026

    Modern Vintage Wave (Psicolabel): 10 songs picked from about 30 unreleased recordings made between 2008 and 2025.

The band

Stage name · real name

Charlie Out

Carlo Casale · vocals

Co-founder. Ran Bassano's Shindy club for twenty years.

Steve Hill / Stewie

Stefano Dal Col · guitar

Co-founder. Spent about ten years in Cuba working in live sound and production.

J.M. Le Baptiste

Maurizio Battistella · drums

With the band since the Trash years.

Mark Brenda

Marco Breda · keyboards

Original keyboardist and a big part of the band's sound.

Also played with the band: Franco Turesso (keyboards), Diego Negrello (bass), Alex Strax (sax), Steve Elbow (bass). On the 2026 album: Marco Greco (bass), Diego Piotto (guitar), Giorgio Canali.
